source.check: returned without a contest: the 1936 nominations left 'only two changes in the personnel of the old Board' (Kells and Lisnagarron) (Ballymena Observer, 8 May 1936, p. 10); George Elder sits on the new council from June 1936 and is named as the retiring member for Ballyscullion in 1939 (Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1939, p. 10), which ties him to the division for the 1936-39 term

note: Triennial election of Ballymena Rural District Council (and Guardians); nominations received on Wednesday 6 May 1936 by Mr. John Leckey, clerk and returning officer. 'There were only two changes in the personnel of the old Board, viz., in the Kells division, where Joseph Maybin, junr., was nominated in the room of his father, Mr. Joseph Maybin, J.P., and in the Lisnagarron division where Wm. H. Simpson was nominated in the place of his father, Hugh Simpson. Only 18 nominations were received out of the 23 electoral divisions, leaving 5 divisions viz. Tullygarley, Toome, Dunminning, Newtowncrommelin, and Ballyconnelly, as they were, so that the old members for these divisions were declared returned' (Ballymena Observer, 8 May 1936, p. 10, image-read). No poll; the statutory polling day in Co. Antrim was Thursday 4 June 1936. Only the two new members are named in the report, so only Kells and Lisnagarron are recorded (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Ahoghill, Ballyclug, Ballyconnolly, Broughshane, Clough, Cloughogue, Crumkill, Dunminning, Galgorm, Glenbuck, Glenravel, Glenwherry, Kirkinriola, Longmore, Newtowncrommelin, Portglenone, Slemish, Toome and Tullygarley. Ballyscullion and Drumanaway (round 2, 7 Nov 2026): George Elder and John M'Ateer, members of the old Board after the 1933 members died, sit on the new council from June-July 1936 and are named as the retiring members for those divisions in 1939 (Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1939, p. 10). The 1933 member died during the term and the council filled the place; the successor was returned unopposed in 1936 as one of the old Board. The division was not among the five without a nomination (Tullygarley, Toome, Dunminning, Newtowncrommelin, Ballyconnelly), so he was the sole nominee, but the 1936 report does not print his name. Returned unopposed.
